US hiring plans continue to improve:

US-based employers announced plans to hire 12,325 workers in August, the strongest August total since 2022.

This marks a +725% increase from the 1,494 recorded in August 2025.

Aerospace and Defense led all industries, with 4,025 announced hires, followed by Technology at 2,520, and Industrial Goods at 1,856.

Year-to-date, US hiring plans surged +37% YoY, to 119,825 workers, the strongest January-to-August total since 2023.

Technology leads all sectors with 19,751 announcements so far in 2026, followed by Aerospace and Defense, at 16,541, and Automotive, at 14,937.

Meanwhile, manufacturing industries now account for 46% of all announced hiring plans this year.

Hiring plans are gaining momentum.

BREAKING: Global central banks purchased +23 tonnes of gold in July, marking their 4th consecutive monthly purchase.

This follows +51 tonnes in June, their 2nd-largest monthly purchase since November 2024.

In July, demand was led by China at +20 tonnes, bringing its year-to-date purchases to +60 tonnes.

Poland followed with +8 tonnes, lifting its total 2026 purchases to +90 tonnes.

Year-to-date, central banks have acquired +130 tonnes of gold, slightly trailing the +160 tonnes purchased over the same period last year.

Meanwhile, the Bank of Korea disclosed on August 13th that it made its first gold investment in 13 years, holding $250 million in the largest US gold-backed ETF, $GLD, as of Q2 2026.

Central bank gold demand remains incredibly strong.

World Labs co-founder Justin Johnson says Atlas can recreate the famous "Bullet Time" shot from The Matrix with iPhones:

"The way they did that shot is they had a ring of hundreds of cameras. [Neo] fell over in the studio, they had hundreds of cameras viewing that angle on a green screen, and then they used those hundreds and hundreds of cameras to make that famous shot in The Matrix."

"Now with Atlas, we can do this with as few as three cameras. No studio capture, no green screen, no expensive calibration. We can literally stick three iPhones on tripods and use these to take video of something happening."

"From those three iPhone videos, we can then reframe the shot and imagine, like, freeze time, have the camera fly in as the milk is splashing up, and get these amazing frozen-time views. We can do this with just a couple cameras."

@jcjohnss

BREAKING: South Korea's exports surged +72.5% YoY in August, their largest annual increase on record.

This follows a +63.0% gain in July and marks the 2nd consecutive monthly improvement.

South Korean exports have now seen above +40.0% YoY growth for 7-straight months.

Semiconductor exports continue to lead the gains, surging +209.0% YoY, to $46.7 billion, driven by strong AI and data center investments.

At the same time, shipments of computer-related products soared +419.0%.

By destination, exports rose +119.0% to China, +89.3% to the US, +47.3% to India, and +14.6% to the EU.

South Korea has become a global economic power.

So we asked RV Brain the real question: with this much cash still in the system, can a rate move even touch the market?

Its read: liquidity decides the trend. The rate only decides the shock.

A hike bites only if it drains real cash. If the system's still awash, growth stocks and real estate take the hit while the broader trend holds.

New question every week. What should we ask it next?

RV Brain reads everything inside Real Vision: every interview, analyst call and research note in the archive.

Renewed US strikes on Iran pushed oil back above $95, and oil is a tax on everything, so bonds repriced inflation everywhere at once.

Palvatar breaks down why this is one global debt story in yesterday's recap.

The personal saving rate fell to 3.0% in July, near the lowest since 2022, while the Fed floods the system with new money. Asset owners get richer, the median household runs on fumes.

A consumer with no buffer cracks the moment a job or a credit line disappears. When the cushion is gone, defensive staples tend to outrun discretionary. $XLP

M2 money supply is growing close to 5% a year, the fastest since 2022, and sits at a record above $22 trillion. In 2023 it shrank for the first time in decades, and that is exactly when goods inflation cooled.

Now the Fed is cutting rates and buying Treasuries while the money supply re-accelerates. Tariffs and wages move single prices. This line moves the price level.

The next inflation wave is being printed right now. Own the assets that get repriced, not the cash that gets debased.

The median American homebuyer is now 59 years old. In 1981 it was 31.

The 30-year mortgage is stuck near 6.7%, about half of all outstanding mortgages carry a rate under 4%, and the payment on a new loan runs roughly $2,918 a month.

Nobody trades a 3% mortgage for a 7% one, so existing homes never reach the market and new construction becomes the only option. That is why homebuilders keep taking share while resales stay frozen. $XHB

A poor Louisiana farming parish just watched its average weekly wage nearly double.

Meta's data center pushed private wages in Richland Parish up 61% and employment up 41% in a single year. Construction pay jumped 182%, an $86,000 raise, with the building workforce up more than 10-fold.

On Wall Street the AI boom is a chip multiple. In Richland Parish it is a paycheck. The buildout is physical, and the money lands in power, steel, and construction, which is why the picks-and-shovels keep running.

Germany funds its pensions with 7% of GDP. Canada does it with 185%.

The least-funded system in the developed world is finally reforming. It will channel 2% of pay into long-term savings and build toward roughly 90 billion euros a year, about 2% of GDP, by the early 2030s.

That is a recurring, decade-long bid landing under European stocks and credit, in a market that has starved for domestic capital. It is the structural fuel behind the European re-rating.

$EWG
